currentContext.business: The Rico Group is engaged in the design, development, manufacturing and supply of high-precision, engineering-grade aluminium and ferrous components and assemblies for the global automotive industry, with integrated capabilities spanning product design, tooling, casting, precision machining and assembly. It produces engine and transmission parts, braking systems and other critical components for two-wheelers, passenger vehicles and commercial vehicles, and its product portfolio supports Hybrid Vehicles, Electric Vehicles (EVs) and Internal Combustion Engines (ICEs). Incorporated in 1983, the Group operates 16 manufacturing plants with 6,000+ employees and a presence in 4 continents, and has created a non-auto vertical focused on Railways and manufacturing of CNC machines.

currentContext.expansion: The headline expansion is a new greenfield plant at Hosur, listed as the Company's 2026 key milestone and shown in the Manufacturing Locations spread as an 'Upcoming Manufacturing Plant'. The Directors' Report states that readiness of the new facility at SIPCOT Industrial Park, Shoolagiri, Hosur, Tamil Nadu is in progress and that commercial production is expected to start during Q3 of the current financial year, catering to the requirements of Toyota, AISIN and other OEMs in the southern region primarily for Hybrid and EVs; the facility is described as aligned towards next-gen mobility manufacturing and is said to contribute to the Company's vision of 3X growth. The Group operates 16 manufacturing plants (16 plants and 1 office nationally per BRSR Section A), and management says the facilities are geographically spread and strategically located to de-risk operations, with various new businesses launched for optimum utilisation of existing capacities. Renewable capacity continues to be added at the plants: captive solar at Gurugram (10 MW), solar and wind at Chennai (3.5 MW), rooftop solar at Bawal (1.40 MW), at Rico Jinfei Wheels Manesar (450 KW), at Pathredi (1000 KW) and at Haridwar (500 KW). On the technology side, the Company scaled Industry 4.0 initiatives, expanding robotics, automated inspection and gauging technologies and integrated material handling systems, and IoT-enabled real-time monitoring. R&D spend for 2025-26 comprised capital expenditure of Rs 4.70 crore and operating expenditure of Rs 10.63 crore, a total of Rs 15.33 crore as printed in the Section 134(3)(m) annexure. In BRSR Principle 2 the Group reports that 0.64% of total capex in FY 2025-26 (4.11% in FY 2024-25) went into technologies improving environmental and social impact - wet scrubbers for air emissions, ETP and STP systems with RO and ultrafiltration, and natural gas detection systems - and 26.27% of R&D investment (22.28% in FY 2024-25) into such technologies. Prior expansion milestones recorded in the AR include the 2013 non-auto vertical (Railways, CNC machine manufacturing), the 2014 acquisition of a 70% stake in Rico Friction Technologies, and the earlier addition of the Bawal, Pathredi, Chennai, Halol, Bhiwadi, Sanand, Haridwar and Manesar plants.

risks.risk: Complex, fast-changing operating environment across manufacturing and distribution
risks.note: MD&A Risks & Concerns: evolving market conditions, global supply chain interdependencies, changing customer expectations, stringent regulatory requirements and operational risks across the manufacturing and distribution network; macroeconomic developments, geopolitical events, technological advancements and industry-specific trends bear on business performance. Managed through an Enterprise Risk Management framework with Key Risk Indicators covering market dynamics, supply chain resilience, operational excellence, quality, regulatory compliance, cybersecurity, information security, financial controls and business continuity.

Directors' Report: aluminium and other raw material prices remained volatile due to fluctuation in the global commodity market; healthy demand conditions and the customer pass-through mechanism limited the effect on margins, so the exposure is structural and dependent on that pass-through continuing to work.

risks.risk: Climate change - energy cost and regulatory pressure
risks.note: BRSR material issue: high energy consumption and associated emissions from manufacturing operations expose the Group to rising energy costs and regulatory pressures; mitigation is an integrated energy management framework, energy efficiency measures, cleaner technologies, renewable energy procurement, fuel transition and process electrification.

risks.risk: Emissions management and OEM decarbonisation requirements
risks.note: BRSR material issue (rated Risk, financial implication Negative): increasingly stringent emissions norms, evolving carbon pricing mechanisms and heightened stakeholder expectations can materially increase compliance costs and constrain market access, particularly with global OEM customers advancing decarbonisation commitments.

risks.risk: Responsible supply chain / ESG oversight of suppliers
risks.note: BRSR material issue: insufficient oversight of ESG practices within the supply chain exposes the Group to reputational damage, regulatory non-compliance and operational disruptions with direct implications for OEM customers, suppliers, investors and regulators; mitigated through the Supplier Code of Conduct and an ESG-based supplier evaluation framework under development.

BRSR material issue: unsafe or inadequately controlled working conditions can result in workplace incidents, regulatory penalties, diminished morale and reputational harm, disrupt operations and affect OEM customers who apply rigorous responsible supply chain standards; mitigated by an ISO 45001-aligned OH&S management system, safety training, risk assessments, mock drills, audits and PPE compliance.

BRSR material issue: inadequate waste management exposes the Group to soil and water contamination, non-compliance penalties and increased disposal costs; mitigated by segregation at source and disposal through authorised recyclers.

risks.risk: Workforce attrition, particularly among permanent workers
risks.note: BRSR Section A item 22: turnover rate for permanent workers rose to 58.60% in FY 2025-26 from 18.69% in FY 2024-25 (25.66% in FY 2023-24), and for permanent employees to 42.72% from 40.75%. The Company also notes reliance on emerging workforce models including Fixed Term Employment, and that 4,174 of 5,980 workers are other-than-permanent.

one-line thesis: Highest-ever FY26 revenue (INR2,477 cr, +12%) with FY27 guided to cross INR3,000 cr (~21%+) on ~40 new program launches (single-source, INR2,500 cr / 5-yr order book), normalized FY26 EBITDA margin of 10.25% (vs 9% reported, dragged by INR19 cr RM lag + INR11 cr Labour Code one-offs) protected and biased higher into FY27 — plus emerging Railways/Defence/CNC-machine-tool optionality — though net debt remains elevated (INR686 cr, ~3.75x leverage).
financial scorecard:
**Consolidated, INR cr (reported):**
- **Q4 FY26 revenue:** 677 (incl. exports 102); EBITDA 47.8, margin 7.1% (mgmt also cited 7.6% on different base); PAT 6.9.
  - *Normalized Q4 EBITDA margin:* ~9.8% after adding back Labour Code INR3.6 cr + RM lag-settlement INR11.22 cr. (Mgmt elsewhere referenced ~9.5% adjusted Q4 — slight inconsistency.)
- **FY26 revenue:** 2,477, **+12% YoY** — highest ever (incl. exports 395).
- **FY26 EBITDA:** 223, margin **9.0%**; **normalized FY26 margin 10.25%** (vs 9% last year) after excluding Labour Code INR11 cr + RM lag-settlement INR19 cr.
- **FY26 PAT:** 52.4 vs 19.2 last year (~2.7x).
- **Gross margin:** not disclosed explicitly; sharp Q4 gross-margin decline flagged by analyst, attributed to RM lag + Labour Code one-offs.
- **Net debt (Mar'26):** 686 vs 653.1 prior year (rose YoY); leverage ~3.75x. Working-capital days improved to **7 days from 33**; CFO INR331 cr.
- **One-offs (non-recurring):** Labour Code — INR3.6 cr Q4 / INR11 cr FY26; RM lag-settlement — INR11 cr Q4 / INR19 cr FY26. Recovery of FY26 lag-losses being negotiated separately (would flow straight to bottom line if won).
- **Export share:** 16% of FY26 revenue (vs 15% LY); exports INR395 cr. **EV revenue share: not quantified** (EV/hybrid is order-pipeline/future, not a disclosed current revenue line).
guidance (critical):
- **Revenue:** FY27 to **cross INR3,000 cr** (~21–25% growth off INR2,477 cr) — driven by ~40 new single-source launches, not just market growth.
- **Margin:** FY26 normalized 10.25% is "protected" (75% of customers by value agreed to monthly RM settlement); FY27 expected **above 10.25%**; 10%+ margin from Q1 FY27 onwards. Additional upside if prior-year lag-loss recovery negotiations succeed.
- **Exports:** guided to grow **~32% this year** (FY27), primarily Germany + USA; export to US/Germany to **2x over next 2 years**.
- **EV/hybrid mix:** Hosur plant (operational Sep-2026) "primarily caters to hybrid and EV-related programs" — no explicit EV revenue % target given.
- **Capex/commissioning:** Hosur facility operational from **Sep 2026**; Tamil Nadu subsidy ~INR39 cr approved, accruing from FY27 over 10 years.
- **Railways:** target to cross **INR100 cr in FY27** (vs ~INR3–4 cr FY26); **Defence** target to cross **INR50 cr** (vs ~INR20–30 cr), double over 2 yrs.
order book & pipeline:
- **New orders ~INR2,500 cr** over a 5-year program life (~INR500 cr/yr run-rate target).
- Programs across transmission, braking, engine and EV-related applications.
- New/expanded customers cited: **Toyota, Maruti Suzuki, Hero, Bosch, Cummins, Knorr-Bremse**.
- ~40 product launches underway (single-source), revenue flowing from FY27, peaking FY28; impact "end of Q3 to Q4" FY27.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Aluminium business:** INR2,155 cr FY26, ~**88%** of revenue.
- **Ferrous (iron):** INR322 cr FY26, ~**12%** of revenue.
- **Exports:** 16% of FY26 (US + Germany focus).
- **Capacity utilisation:** Iron ~65–75%; Aluminium similar — small-tonnage machines ~95% util, higher-tonnage machines have freed capacity to absorb new components.
- **Railways:** FY26 only ~INR3–4 cr; products = bearing adapters, LC cast-iron inserts, track adjusters, distance blocks. RDSO approvals received for 3–5 of 7–8 assemblies; first lot dispatched ~late May'26.
- **Defence:** ~INR20–30 cr; mainly shooting ranges, expanding portfolio.
- **CNC machine tools:** historically captive (5/8/14/16-axis); now selling externally — first external sale just made; figures next quarter.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Hybrid/EV components** — Hosur plant dedicated to hybrid + EV programs for key OEMs (Sep-2026).
- **Railways** — modernization tailwind (mgmt cites ~INR2,00,000 cr railway investment); minimal incremental capex, uses existing capacity; higher margin than auto.
- **Defence** — slower (sensitive testing/clearances) but scaling.
- **CNC machine-tool external sales** — new optionality, unquantified.
- **Land monetization** — plant land; prior bid of INR700 cr rejected, seeking better value; could conclude within 6 months or not at all (potential shareholder reward event).
margins & cost dynamics:
- Aluminium / RM prices volatile in FY26; customer pass-through "with limited effect on margins," but **lag** in quarterly settlement caused the INR19 cr FY26 drag.
- Fix: shifting RM settlement to **monthly** — 75% of customers (by value) agreed → protects 10.25%.
- Also renegotiating conversion-cost inflation (oil, gas, imported consumables hit by INR depreciation) and culling low-margin products across portfolio.
- Railways/Defence margins better than auto (specifics pending 1–2 quarters).
capex / expansion:
- **Hosur** plant — investment "progressing as planned," operational **Sep-2026**, for hybrid/EV programs. **Watch for slippage** (prior Railways/Defence revenue targets slipped due to approval delays).
- TN govt subsidy ~INR39 cr over 10 years, accruing FY27.
- Land/buildings investment for current programs began 1–2 yrs ago; revenue now fructifying.
capital allocation:
- **Net debt INR686 cr** (up YoY from 653.1); leverage ~3.75x.
- Scheduled repayments **~INR110–120 cr/yr over next 3 years** — "downward gliding path."
- Working capital sharply improved (7 days vs 33). No dividend commentary on this call.
- Potential land sale as deleveraging / shareholder-reward catalyst.
risks & watch-items:
- **Net debt elevated** (~3.75x); deleveraging dependent on EBITDA growth + scheduled repayments (and possibly land sale).
- **RM lag recovery uncertain** — INR19 cr FY26 loss recovery only "parallelly going on," not booked.
- **Aggressive FY27 guidance** (>INR3,000 cr / ~21%+) vs OEM industry growth of 5–8% — relies on ~40 launches ramping on schedule (execution/launch-timing risk).
- **Execution slippage track record** — Railways/Defence FY26 missed prior INR60–70 cr guidance due to approval delays.
- OEM/customer concentration; commodity (aluminium) and FX (INR) cost inflation.
- EV transition pace — Hosur tied to hybrid/EV ramp at OEMs.
management quality / tone: Confident and candid. Transparent on one-off bridge (reported 9% → normalized 10.25%) and on the structural fix (monthly RM settlement, 75% agreed). Honest admission that FY26 Railways/Defence targets were missed on approval delays. Concrete numbers on order book, capex, leverage. Slight internal inconsistency on Q4 adjusted margin (9.5% vs 9.8%). Forward export/growth claims are bold and worth tracking against delivery.
non-obvious takeaways:
- Reported margin understates true profitability by ~125 bps (9.0% → 10.25%); FY27 starts from a cleaner, higher base from Q1.
- Growth is **structural/share-gain + single-source new programs**, not cyclical OEM volume — decoupled from the modest 5–8% industry growth.
- **Railways is the near-term surprise lever** (INR3–4 cr → INR100 cr target, higher margin, minimal capex on existing capacity).
- **Land monetization** (>INR700 cr rejected; mkt cap context relevant) is a potentially large, under-appreciated balance-sheet/shareholder catalyst.
- CNC machine-tool external sales = new, optional revenue stream.
- Despite "EV-agnostic" framing, EV is still pipeline-only — no current EV revenue disclosure; Hosur is the EV/hybrid proof point.

- **Gross margin:** not disclosed explicitly; sharp Q4 gross-margin decline flagged by analyst, attributed to RM lag + Labour Code one-offs.
- **Net debt (Mar'26):** 686 vs 653.1 prior year (rose YoY); leverage ~3.75x. Working-capital days improved to **7 days from 33**; CFO INR331 cr.
- **One-offs (non-recurring):** Labour Code — INR3.6 cr Q4 / INR11 cr FY26; RM lag-settlement — INR11 cr Q4 / INR19 cr FY26. Recovery of FY26 lag-losses being negotiated separately (would flow straight to bottom line if won).
- **Export share:** 16% of FY26 revenue (vs 15% LY); exports INR395 cr. **EV revenue share: not quantified** (EV/hybrid is order-pipeline/future, not a disclosed current revenue line).
guidance (critical):
- **Revenue:** FY27 to **cross INR3,000 cr** (~21–25% growth off INR2,477 cr) — driven by ~40 new single-source launches, not just market growth.
- **Margin:** FY26 normalized 10.25% is "protected" (75% of customers by value agreed to monthly RM settlement); FY27 expected **above 10.25%**; 10%+ margin from Q1 FY27 onwards. Additional upside if prior-year lag-loss recovery negotiations succeed.
- **Exports:** guided to grow **~32% this year** (FY27), primarily Germany + USA; export to US/Germany to **2x over next 2 years**.
- **EV/hybrid mix:** Hosur plant (operational Sep-2026) "primarily caters to hybrid and EV-related programs" — no explicit EV revenue % target given.
- **Capex/commissioning:** Hosur facility operational from **Sep 2026**; Tamil Nadu subsidy ~INR39 cr approved, accruing from FY27 over 10 years.
- **Railways:** target to cross **INR100 cr in FY27** (vs ~INR3–4 cr FY26); **Defence** target to cross **INR50 cr** (vs ~INR20–30 cr), double over 2 yrs.
order book & pipeline:
- **New orders ~INR2,500 cr** over a 5-year program life (~INR500 cr/yr run-rate target).
- Programs across transmission, braking, engine and EV-related applications.
- New/expanded customers cited: **Toyota, Maruti Suzuki, Hero, Bosch, Cummins, Knorr-Bremse**.
- ~40 product launches underway (single-source), revenue flowing from FY27, peaking FY28; impact "end of Q3 to Q4" FY27.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Aluminium business:** INR2,155 cr FY26, ~**88%** of revenue.
- **Ferrous (iron):** INR322 cr FY26, ~**12%** of revenue.
- **Exports:** 16% of FY26 (US + Germany focus).
- **Capacity utilisation:** Iron ~65–75%; Aluminium similar — small-tonnage machines ~95% util, higher-tonnage machines have freed capacity to absorb new components.
- **Railways:** FY26 only ~INR3–4 cr; products = bearing adapters, LC cast-iron inserts, track adjusters, distance blocks. RDSO approvals received for 3–5 of 7–8 assemblies; first lot dispatched ~late May'26.
- **Defence:** ~INR20–30 cr; mainly shooting ranges, expanding portfolio.
- **CNC machine tools:** historically captive (5/8/14/16-axis); now selling externally — first external sale just made; figures next quarter.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Hybrid/EV components** — Hosur plant dedicated to hybrid + EV programs for key OEMs (Sep-2026).
- **Railways** — modernization tailwind (mgmt cites ~INR2,00,000 cr railway investment); minimal incremental capex, uses existing capacity; higher margin than auto.
- **Defence** — slower (sensitive testing/clearances) but scaling.
- **CNC machine-tool external sales** — new optionality, unquantified.
- **Land monetization** — plant land; prior bid of INR700 cr rejected, seeking better value; could conclude within 6 months or not at all (potential shareholder reward event).
margins & cost dynamics:
- Aluminium / RM prices volatile in FY26; customer pass-through "with limited effect on margins," but **lag** in quarterly settlement caused the INR19 cr FY26 drag.
- Fix: shifting RM settlement to **monthly** — 75% of customers (by value) agreed → protects 10.25%.
- Also renegotiating conversion-cost inflation (oil, gas, imported consumables hit by INR depreciation) and culling low-margin products across portfolio.
- Railways/Defence margins better than auto (specifics pending 1–2 quarters).
capex / expansion:
- **Hosur** plant — investment "progressing as planned," operational **Sep-2026**, for hybrid/EV programs. **Watch for slippage** (prior Railways/Defence revenue targets slipped due to approval delays).
- TN govt subsidy ~INR39 cr over 10 years, accruing FY27.
- Land/buildings investment for current programs began 1–2 yrs ago; revenue now fructifying.
capital allocation:
- **Net debt INR686 cr** (up YoY from 653.1); leverage ~3.75x.
- Scheduled repayments **~INR110–120 cr/yr over next 3 years** — "downward gliding path."
- Working capital sharply improved (7 days vs 33). No dividend commentary on this call.
- Potential land sale as deleveraging / shareholder-reward catalyst.
risks & watch-items:
- **Net debt elevated** (~3.75x); deleveraging dependent on EBITDA growth + scheduled repayments (and possibly land sale).
- **RM lag recovery uncertain** — INR19 cr FY26 loss recovery only "parallelly going on," not booked.
- **Aggressive FY27 guidance** (>INR3,000 cr / ~21%+) vs OEM industry growth of 5–8% — relies on ~40 launches ramping on schedule (execution/launch-timing risk).
- **Execution slippage track record** — Railways/Defence FY26 missed prior INR60–70 cr guidance due to approval delays.
- OEM/customer concentration; commodity (aluminium) and FX (INR) cost inflation.
- EV transition pace — Hosur tied to hybrid/EV ramp at OEMs.
management quality / tone: Confident and candid. Transparent on one-off bridge (reported 9% → normalized 10.25%) and on the structural fix (monthly RM settlement, 75% agreed). Honest admission that FY26 Railways/Defence targets were missed on approval delays. Concrete numbers on order book, capex, leverage. Slight internal inconsistency on Q4 adjusted margin (9.5% vs 9.8%). Forward export/growth claims are bold and worth tracking against delivery.
non-obvious takeaways:
- Reported margin understates true profitability by ~125 bps (9.0% → 10.25%); FY27 starts from a cleaner, higher base from Q1.
- Growth is **structural/share-gain + single-source new programs**, not cyclical OEM volume — decoupled from the modest 5–8% industry growth.
- **Railways is the near-term surprise lever** (INR3–4 cr → INR100 cr target, higher margin, minimal capex on existing capacity).
- **Land monetization** (>INR700 cr rejected; mkt cap context relevant) is a potentially large, under-appreciated balance-sheet/shareholder catalyst.
- CNC machine-tool external sales = new, optional revenue stream.
- Despite "EV-agnostic" framing, EV is still pipeline-only — no current EV revenue disclosure; Hosur is the EV/hybrid proof point.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.

themes.title: Auto OEM cycle - CV replacement & PV premiumization
themes.need: GST 2.0 rate rationalization plus an aged CV fleet still frames the replacement cycle, but Q1FY27's real signal is 2W OEMs EXPANDING margin through a commodity shock. TVSMOTOR sold 1.63mn units (+28%) on INR 13,896cr revenue (+38%) while lifting EBITDA margin 30bps to 12.8% having absorbed a ~4% commodity shock with only ~1.5% of price increase (CARE upgraded it AA+ to AAA), and committed 2W capacity from 6.8mn to 8.3mn by Q4FY27. BAJAJ-AUTO set volume/revenue/EBITDA records with margin at 20.9% (+110bps) through ~4.5% commodity inflation AND ~10% of volume lost to a ransomware shutdown, with EV now 30% of domestic revenue at double-digit EBITDA and Chetak EBITDA-positive - a scaled, profitable EV second engine. Commercial mobility is electrifying fastest: TVSMOTOR's 3W EV penetration crossed 40% for the first time. ASHOKLEY's all-time-high CV volumes (220k units, MHCV share 30.8%) carry the CV leg with defence + Switch EV optionality; TMCV/TMPV/SMLMAH/ESCORTS on CV/tractors; APOLLOTYRE/JKTYRE/BALKRISIND/MRF on tyres.
themes.driver: Capacity commissioning against demand (TVSMOTOR 2W to 8.3mn by Q4FY27, BAJAJ-AUTO 7m to 9m+ units); 3W/2W EV penetration inflection; GST-2.0 price-cut demand, aged-fleet replacement and festive 2W/PV.
